CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

c. to provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women carried out by Regional Apparatus that administer governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

Integrated Service is the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women and children protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEBUMEN REGENCY

CONCERNING
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

1.1.rationale: The original Indonesian text does explicitly cover violence occurring in the domestic/private sphere, which is the core of “domestic violence” scope. Article 1 point 13 defines “Kekerasan Terhadap Perempuan” as violence that occurs “baik yang terjadi di ranah privat atau publik” (whether in the private or public sphere). In addition, Article 1 point 19 defines “Rumah Tangga” (household) and point 18 defines “Keluarga” (family), which supports that the regulation contemplates violence in domestic contexts. These exact elements were present in the retrieved English candidates ([1.1-3] includes ‘private or public sphere’ and the household/family definitions). The judge incorrectly required an explicit label like “domestic violence/intimate partner violence” as a distinct category, even though the policy’s inclusion of the private sphere and household context satisfies the indicator’s scope requirement.

1.10.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation does address technology-facilitated violence, at least in the form of electronic-based sexual violence and remedies related to online content. Article 1 point 17 explicitly includes “kekerasan seksual berbasis elektronik” (electronic-based sexual violence) within the definition of sexual violence. Article 6(2) letter g provides a right to “penghapusan konten bermuatan seksual untuk kasus kekerasan seksual dengan media elektronik” (removal of sexually charged content for sexual violence cases using electronic media). These are direct mentions of technology/electronic-media-facilitated sexual violence and response measures. Since the judge’s cited English snippets match the Indonesian meaning, the predicted “Yes” is consistent with the source text; therefore the golden label “No” appears incorrect for this document.

5.3.evaluator_rationale: While the text mentions community leaders and local cultural organizations in an arts/culture context, it does not explicitly reference traditional/customary leaders or customary mechanisms for prevention, protection, services, coordination, or dispute resolution.

CONCERNING
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. 6.7.rationale: The judge treated “women in situations of intolerance” (Article 9(3) letter k: “perempuan dalam situasi intoleransi”) as evidence of “women from minority groups,” but the Indonesian text does not explicitly identify minority groups (e.g., ethnic/religious minorities) as a target group. “Situasi intoleransi” describes a context (intolerance situations) rather than naming minority identities, and the regulation’s non-discrimination principle (Pasal 2 and its Elucidation) is general rather than an intersectional commitment to minority women. The retrieved passages contained exactly this limited phrasing, so the judge’s inference was too broad/lenient given the indicator’s focus on minority-group women.
